title: DyLeCT: Achieving Huge-page-like Translation Performance for Hardware-compressed Memory
problem: Hardware memory compression requires an additional translation layer in the memory controller, which can double TLB translation misses for workloads with frequent page-level address translation. While huge pages reduce TLB misses, moving entire huge pages of compressed data together consumes excessive memory bandwidth.
motivation: Enabling efficient hardware memory compression for large irregular workloads by achieving huge-page-like translation performance without the bandwidth overhead.
method: DyLeCT dynamically assigns variable-length translation entries based on page hotness: hot pages are migrated to limited DRAM locations with short entries (e.g., 2 bits), while cold pages retain full-length translations for flexible placement anywhere in memory. A 128KB translation cache containing mostly short entries achieves similar translation reach (2GB) as a TLB filled entirely with huge page entries.
key_novelty: Using dynamic-length compression on address translation entries where hot pages confined to restricted address ranges use minimal-bit encoding, while cold pages retain full-length translations.
contributions: Identifies that hardware memory compression doubles translation misses for irregular workloads
Proposes dynamic-length translation mechanism adapting entry size to page hotness for compressed memory
Achieves huge-page-like translation performance at page granularity without huge-page bandwidth costs
Demonstrates 10.25% average performance improvement over prior compression approaches
limitations: Specific workload characteristics, energy consumption, and area overhead not discussed in abstract
